# Task 01 — Explanation

## Mental model

Think of an Astro Content Collection as a structured content source.

~~~text
Markdown files
      ↓
Content Collection
      ↓
getCollection()
      ↓
array of entries
      ↓
.map()
      ↓
ResourceCard.astro
~~~

`getCollection()` returns entries. Your custom fields live inside `entry.data`.

Example:

~~~js
{
  id: "astro-routing",
  data: {
    title: "Understanding Astro Routing",
    topic: "Astro",
    readingTime: 7
  }
}
~~~

So you read:

~~~js
resource.data.title
~~~

not:

~~~js
resource.title
~~~

## Why split the components?

The page should coordinate data and page structure.

`ResourcesGrid.astro` owns the list.

`ResourceCard.astro` owns the markup for one resource.

That makes the card reusable later on:

- Home page
- Resources page
- Related content
- Search results

## Why Content Collections instead of a JSON import?

A JSON array is fine for simple data.

Content Collections become more useful when your content grows because they give you:

- a consistent content API
- loaders
- schemas/type safety
- Markdown/MDX support
- easier migration to CMS-driven content

## Why container queries?

A viewport media query asks:

> How wide is the browser?

A container query asks:

> How much space does this component actually have?

That is useful when the same card can appear in different layouts.

## Interview questions

### Why is `ResourceCard.astro` separate from the page?

A strong answer:

The page handles data loading and composition, while the card encapsulates repeated presentation. This avoids duplicated markup and makes the card reusable.

### Why use `getCollection()`?

A strong answer:

It gives Astro a structured way to retrieve all entries from a named content collection and works consistently across different content loaders.

### Why avoid JavaScript for the hover animation?

A strong answer:

The interaction is purely visual, so CSS is simpler, cheaper, and avoids unnecessary client-side JavaScript.

# Task 01 — Reusable Content Section

## Goal

Build a `Latest Resources` section powered by an Astro Content Collection.

The page must render resource cards from content files instead of hard-coded HTML.

## You will practice

- `content.config.ts`
- `defineCollection()`
- `glob()`
- `getCollection()`
- Astro component props
- `.map()`
- conditional classes
- reusable components
- content vs presentation separation

## Required structure

~~~text
src/
├── content/
│   └── resources/
│       ├── astro-routing.md
│       ├── css-container-queries.md
│       └── array-methods.md
├── components/
│   ├── ResourceCard.astro
│   └── ResourcesGrid.astro
└── content.config.ts
~~~

Each resource must have:

- title
- description
- topic
- reading time
- featured boolean

## UI

Show a responsive grid of cards.

Each card should display:

- topic
- title
- description
- reading time
- arrow/action affordance

The featured card should look different without creating a second card component.

## CSS practice

Use:

- CSS Grid
- `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(...))`
- `clamp()`
- `aspect-ratio`
- container queries
- pseudo-elements
- subtle gradient decoration
- `:focus-visible`
- `prefers-reduced-motion`

## Interaction

On hover/focus:

- card lifts slightly
- gradient/border becomes more visible
- arrow moves a few pixels
- media area scales slightly

Prefer `transform` and `opacity`.

## Acceptance criteria

- No resource is hard-coded in `index.astro`.
- Data comes from `getCollection('resources')`.
- `ResourceCard.astro` receives one resource through props.
- Adding a fourth Markdown file creates a fourth card automatically.
- Featured state uses the same card component.
- Keyboard focus is visible.
- Layout works on mobile and desktop.
- `npm run build` succeeds.

## Hints

1. Configure the collection before styling anything.
2. Temporarily log the result of `getCollection('resources')` to inspect its shape.
3. Remember: collection fields are under `entry.data`.
4. Keep the card component focused on one item.
5. Use `container-type: inline-size` on the card if you want it to respond to its own width.

## Stretch goals

- Sort featured items first.
- Add `publishedAt` and sort newest first.
- Make the entire card clickable accessibly.
- Create a compact card variant using container queries only.
